text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — KV cache continuous-batch regression detected in prod region us-west-2. Metric: kv_cache.memory_bytes spiked from ~1.2GB to 9.8GB in ~6m, evictions up 8x. Affected routes: /v1/generate (high throughput customers). Paging triggered. Paging channel: #incidents.
ash: ack, I'm on it. paging to SRE + runtime. severity: sev2 for now while we profile impact.
lina: I'm joining — pulling graphs. Noticed a correlation with batch_shaper.feature rollout 2026-03-15T02:14 UTC (canary -> global). Could be continuous batching window expansion.
mike: on runtime. seeing simultaneous long KV write latencies and large KV pages moving to disk. logs show repeated prefix cache misses and huge KV merges.
jia: support observability — queue of open tickets flagged as cost spikes for some customers. Customer-facing docs asked for ETA. We should collect affected tenant list.
ash: initial mitigation plan: 1) put batch_shaper.feature back to canary or reduce window, 2) enable per-tenant batch_override for the top-10 impacted tenants, 3) monitor kv_cache.evictions and tail latencies. Anyone object?
lina: +1. Do we have a fast path to flip the feature? Use flags-ui or redwoodctl?
mike: redwoodctl can flip it across envs. Command: ```redwoodctl feature toggle batch_shaper --env prod --set=false``` But that's global. We can instead set per-tenant: ```redwoodctl feature set-for-tenant batch_shaper tenant=tenant-1234 --value=false``` That requires tenant IDs.
ash: mike, can you list top-20 tenants by kv cache footprint so we can set overrides quickly?
mike: running query now. returning top tenants: tenant-1234, tenant-444, tenant-555, tenant-88, tenant-zelda, tenant-alpha (full list in internal gist). Will paste soon.
oncall-bot: NOTE: Pager duty escalation in 10m if no manual ack by oncall.
ash: I already acked and assigned to "ash". No PD escalation needed now.
jia: I'm messaging CS for tenant-1234 and tenant-444 to say we're investigating and applying mitigations; no user-visible downtime expected but we might throttle aggressive batching for them.
kiran: from CS — they need a short blurb: "We're applying a configuration update to reduce batching window for your traffic to stabilize memory usage. No action required on your side." I'll handle comms once we have a window to share.
mike: quick check: batch_shaper default.window was 2048 tokens, the new rollout sets default.window=8192 for better throughput. That explains cache growth under some long-sequence workloads.
lina: that would massively inflate KV cache sizes. Suggest temporary reduce to 1024 and enable per-tenant override for high-memory tenants.
ash: ok plan: step 0 capture heap profiles. step 1 set per-tenant override for top-10 to 1024. step 2 start a small global canary rollback to default.window=1024 for 5% of traffic. step 3 if stable, roll to 100% or continue per-tenant until safer rollout.
mike: applying per-tenant overrides now. Running commands for batch_shaper:
```
# per-tenant override loop (internal tooling)
for t in tenant-1234 tenant-444 tenant-555 tenant-88 tenant-zelda tenant-alpha tenant-beta tenant-gamma tenant-999 tenant-77; do
  redwoodctl feature set-for-tenant batch_shaper tenant=$t --value.window=1024 || echo "failed $t"
done
```
mike: commands executed, API returned 200 for all except tenant-999 which hit a timeout; retrying.
ash: good. Monitor KV cache metrics for those tenants.
lina: dashboards update: per-tenant memory for tenant-1234 down from 3.2GB to 1.1GB after override — nice.
ash: can we confirm customer request queue for tenant-1234? jia?
jia: tenant-1234 CS confirms they saw sudden cost spike and some 5xxs earlier. I'll keep them updated — next update in 15m.
mike: starting a conservative global canary rollback to default.window=1024 on 5% of requests. Using rollout service: ```deploy-bot rollout-config --feature=batch_shaper --pct=5 --key=default.window=1024``` deploying now.
deployer-bot: Rollout started: batch_shaper default.window=1024 to 5% of traffic. ID: r-20260315-01
ash: observe tail latencies and evictions for the canary group.
lina: canary group looks good so far (6m): evictions down 60% for canary, p95 latency decreased 110ms -> 55ms.
mike: reconnecting logs: small uptick in request latency for canary initially but stable. No increase in errors.
ash: great. Next: increase to 20% if stable for another 10m.
oncall-bot: Reminder: keep channels concise and post status updates at least every 15 minutes.
ash: increasing to 20%.
deployer-bot: Rollout updated: 20% traffic. r-20260315-01 -> 20%.
lina: 12m since 5% -> metrics still improving. Evictions trending down across the board. Per-tenant overrides kept for top tenants.
kiran: CS wants to escalate for tenant-444 — they noted a significant billing delta. Do we want to offer rebate? Hold until final RCA.
jia: noted. I'll collect logs and a short timeline.
mike: one hitch — tenant-999 override failed earlier. I retried and it succeeded. Confirmed all top-10 have overrides.
ash: good. Prepare a postmortem stub. Assign action owners: Mike for runtime fix to prevent future memory amplification; Lina for improved canary guardrails; Ash for oncall runbook updates; Kiran/Jia for customer comms.
lina: adding a short-term guard: we should add a safety throttle that caps cache growth per-tenant to 1.5GB by default. I'll open a doc.
mike: also proposing a runtime change: if KV pages grow > X within Y minutes, reduce batch.window automatically (circuit breaker). I'll draft an implementation PR.
ash: agree — that's much better than global feature flips.
kiran: CS update: I'll send tenant-1234 and tenant-444 an incident notice stating mitigations applied, root cause suspected (batch_shaper default.window increase), and next steps. They asked for ETA for a permanent fix.
ash: postmortem timeline note: root cause = aggressive default.window change landed from canary to global without sufficient workload diversity in canary. Missed signals in canary metrics that would have shown memory growth for long-sequence tenants.
oncall-bot: ACTION: create incident in Jira and link to this thread. Escalation level set to SEV2. Suggested labels: kv-cache, batching, rollout.
ash: I'm creating the Jira now. Jira-INC-4021 created. Link: https://redwood.internal/jira/INC-4021
mike: I pushed a small runtime patch that adds an emergency auto-shrink for batch.window when kv_cache.memory_bytes surge > 3x baseline. PR: https://git.redwood/pr/9876 (hotfix branch: hotfix/kv-batch-shrink). Deploying to prod canary.
deployer-bot: Deployment started for pr-9876 to canary group. Notify when canary success for 20%.
lina: canary for runtime patch looks good. No regressions at 20% after 10m.
ash: rolling runtime patch to 100%.
deployer-bot: Deployment complete for pr-9876 to 100%.
mike: runtime patch live. Monitoring metrics.
lina: kv_cache.memory trending down cluster-wide. Evictions normalized. Tail latencies back to baseline. Good.
ash: closing loop: per-tenant overrides remain for 24h, then we'll remove them gradually after validation unless customers request otherwise.
jia: customer comms sent to top-affected tenants. CS asked for a follow-up meeting tomorrow for compensation discussion if needed.
kiran: noted.
ash: handoff: I'm handing the incident to lina (next on-call) for monitoring for the next 4 hours. Lina, you'll own follow-ups and validate per-tenant rollback schedule.
lina: taking handoff. I'll post hourly updates and coordinate with Mike for any follow-on fixes. Thanks all for quick actions.
ash: thanks team. TL;DR: aggressive batch_shaper.default.window increase caused KV cache blowups for long-sequence tenants -> per-tenant overrides + canary rollback + runtime auto-shrink hotfix stabilized system. Postmortem + runbook PRs incoming.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Status moved to "mitigated". Keep thread open for postmortem drafting.
ash: closing channel for now; will reopen if regressions appear. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
